title: Seva: the guest sails home
hook: the guest sails home with plans for the poor
carry: seva: serve people as you'd serve god

segments.voice: Yesterday, the week came home on a porch by a river: moksha, freedom from what binds. Today, the guest packs up.

A thank-you text, typed and deleted three times, because the real thing is too big for a text. Now a stack of letters, the paper soft from handling. Some go to Chicago, to the family that took a lost monk in off the curb. Some go to India, and those are full of plans: not for a temple, not for a fan club, but for the poor. The guest is packing up, and he's taking what he was given home to give away.
screen: `TOO BIG FOR A TEXT.` → `LETTERS TO CHICAGO, AND TO INDIA.` → `PLANS FOR THE POOR.`

segments.voice: His letters from these years are collected in his Complete Works. To the Hale family in Chicago he writes like one of the household. To friends in India he writes about what he's seen: American schools, and, with real admiration, the education and independence of the women he meets. Then he turns it toward home. India's poor, he writes again and again, have been forgotten, and serving them is the work. Behind that sits a moment with his own teacher. Sri Ramakrishna once said, as his disciples remember it, that pitying people from above isn't enough: serve them as Shiva himself. That's seva, service, and in the Vedanta he taught it's a road to God, because the same divine Self lives in the one who serves and the one who's served. Brother monks came from India to carry on his classes, and he sailed home. In 1897 he founded the Ramakrishna Mission, with a motto it still uses: for one's own liberation, and for the good of the world. So who was the guest, and who was the host? In seva the question melts. Seen that way, the Hales served God in a stranger on their street. He went home to serve God in the poor. Nobody was paying anybody back.
screen: `TO THE HALES, LIKE FAMILY.` · `SERVE THE POOR AS SHIVA.` · `SEVA: GOD IN THE ONE SERVED.` · `WHO WAS GUEST, WHO WAS HOST?`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person who served you this year without being asked: a host, a teacher, a neighbor. If you pray, offer a silent thanks for the God in them. If you don't, just hold their face and wish them well. Then choose one small service for tomorrow, for someone who can't pay you back.
Vivekananda in America: a guest who sailed home to found a mission of seva, serving God in people.
Your line: seva, serve people as you'd serve God. The guest took the gifts home and gave them away. See you tomorrow.
